AI watermarks: what can be removed and what can’t (C2PA, SynthID, ChatGPT text)

People say “AI watermark” for three different things. Only one of them is metadata. Here is an honest breakdown of what ChatGPT, Gemini, Firefly and others add, and what can and can’t be removed.

Updated 2026-11-22 · 6 min read

Open IA Cleaner

1. Metadata “watermarks” (removable)

C2PA Content Credentials, XMP and IPTC fields are records stored next to the image or video data. ChatGPT, Adobe Firefly, Microsoft tools and others write them to say a file was AI-generated. They are what most social networks read to show AI labels, and they can be removed without touching a single pixel — that is exactly what IA Cleaner does.

2. Invisible watermarks (not removable here)

SynthID (Google: Gemini, Imagen, Veo) and similar systems hide a signal in the pixels, audio or word choices themselves. It survives screenshots, cropping and compression and is detected only by the provider’s own tools. It is not metadata, so no metadata cleaner — including IA Cleaner — can see or remove it. Tools that claim to remove it do so by altering the content itself.

3. Visible marks (not removable here)

Logos or icons drawn into the image, like the mark Samsung adds to Galaxy AI edits. They are part of the picture. IA Cleaner does not edit pixels.

What about ChatGPT text?

There is no visible watermark in ChatGPT text. What people find are invisible Unicode characters, citation markers like oaicite and utm_source=chatgpt.com links that come along when you copy. Those are easy to detect and remove — see ChatGPT hidden characters or paste your text in IA Cleaner → Text. Statistical watermarks in word choice, if a provider uses them, can’t be removed by cleaning characters.

Quick summary

  • C2PA, XMP, IPTC, PNG prompts: removable, losslessly.
  • Hidden characters in text: removable.
  • SynthID and other invisible watermarks: not removable with a metadata tool.
  • Visible logos: not removable with a metadata tool.

Use this for privacy and to avoid wrong labels, and disclose AI use where it is required.

What IA Cleaner detects and removes

In photos (JPG, PNG, WebP) it identifies and removes GPS location, camera and phone model, dates, editing apps, XMP and IPTC data, C2PA Content Credentials and embedded AI prompts. Pixels and colour profile stay the same. You see the full report first — every block found, with AI-related ones flagged — and then download the clean copy.
